patients.summary: Thirty-year-old freelance graphic designer with Marfan syndrome and hypertension who joined in August 2024 and dissected his ascending aorta three months later, requiring emergency hemiarch repair. A cocaine-associated diffuse alveolar hemorrhage put him in the ICU in July 2025, and in July 2026 a recurrent Type A dissection of the native root led to a redo valve-sparing root replacement; he is six weeks out with an addiction medicine referral open.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
NEW PATIENT VISIT

CC: Establishing primary care. Needs his BP meds managed going forward.

HPI: 28-year-old man with Marfan syndrome and hypertension. Takes metoprolol succinate 50 mg every morning and lisinopril 10 mg daily, says he rarely misses. Doesn't currently have a cardiologist and isn't sure when his aorta was last imaged. Feels well. No chest or back pain, no palpitations, no exertional shortness of breath, no lightheadedness. Doesn't check BP at home.

PMH: Marfan syndrome. Hypertension.
PSH: None.
Meds: metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily; lisinopril 10 mg daily.
Allergies: penicillin (rash); IV contrast dye (hives).

FH: Father had Marfan syndrome, which was only recognized after he died of an aortic dissection at 42. Paternal aunt has Marfan and had her aortic root replaced electively. Mother with hypertension.

SH: Freelance graphic designer, works from home. Single. Never smoked. Drinks once or twice a month. Medicaid.

ROS: Negative except as above.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Tall and slender, long limbs. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no JVD. Heart regular rate and rhythm, I don't hear a murmur today. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, nontender. Extremities warm, pulses 2+ and equal at both radials, no edema. Skin no rashes.

PHQ-2 0. AUDIT-C 1.

A/P:
1. Marfan syndrome. Family history is heavy (father's dissection, aunt's prophylactic root replacement) and he has no one watching his aorta. Referral to cardiology for surveillance imaging and to take over the aortic side. Continue metoprolol. Reviewed warning signs: sudden chest, back or belly pain = 911, not a phone call.
2. Hypertension. Reasonable today on two drugs. Continue lisinopril 10. BMP.
3. Health maintenance. CBC, lipids. HIV and hep C screening once, he agrees. Flu and COVID shots this fall.

Records release signed for his prior primary care office. Return in about 3 months, sooner after cardiology.

documents.title: Referral Note
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Cardiology referral faxed with today's note and med list. Cardiology scheduling called back: first new-patient slot is mid-December. Pt notified by phone, ok with the date, asked to be put on the cancellation list.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Declan, your labs from yesterday all came back normal: kidney function and potassium are fine on the lisinopril, blood counts normal, cholesterol fine. HIV and hepatitis C screens negative. Nothing to change. Good to meet you.

RECORDS RELEASE — PRIOR PRIMARY CARE OFFICE
Patient: Declan Fischer  DOB 03/16/1996

Problem list: Marfan syndrome. Hypertension.
Medications: metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily. Lisinopril 10 mg daily.
Allergies: Penicillin - rash. Iodinated contrast - hives.

Office notes cover routine hypertension follow-up visits and refills. Blood pressures recorded in an acceptable range on the current regimen. No hospitalizations or surgeries recorded. Immunization record lists childhood series; no recent influenza or tetanus entries on file.

Please contact our records department with any questions.

documents.title: Records Review
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed outside records. Consistent with what he told me: Marfan and HTN on metoprolol/lisinopril, refills and BP checks only. No aortic imaging reports in the packet. Tetanus date unknown, will offer Tdap at a future visit. Cardiology appt in December stands.

documents.title: Nurse Visit - Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body: In for flu and COVID shots. Afebrile, no current illness. Screening questions negative. Allergies reviewed (PCN, contrast) - no vaccine reactions in the past. Flu vaccine L deltoid, COVID vaccine R deltoid. VIS given. Waited 15 min, no reaction. Pt left in good condition.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 11/09/2024

Chief complaint: chest pain

HPI: 28M with Marfan syndrome and HTN, abrupt onset of severe chest pain while at home, describes it as tearing, going straight through to his back, 10/10. Some mild shortness of breath. No cough, no fever, no leg swelling.

Meds: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily.
Allergies: penicillin (rash), contrast dye (urticaria).
FH: father with Marfan, died of aortic dissection at 42; paternal aunt with Marfan s/p prophylactic root replacement; mother HTN.
SH: never smoker, rare alcohol, freelance graphic designer.

Exam: BP 145/90 right arm, 130/85 left arm. HR 110, regular. Tall, thin, long extremities, arachnodactyly, high-arched palate. Diastolic murmur along the right sternal border. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft.

Data: Hgb 14.2, WBC 7.8, plt 250, Cr 1.0, troponin I <0.04. ECG sinus tach, no ischemic changes. Portable CXR with widened mediastinum. Bedside echo: dilated aortic root, aortic regurgitation.

MDM: Presentation is aortic dissection until proven otherwise. CT angiography deferred given documented contrast urticaria and the time cost of premedication; cardiac surgery at bedside within minutes and elected to take him straight to the OR for TEE confirmation.

Disposition: OR, then cardiac surgical ICU.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — CARDIAC SURGERY
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 11/09/2024

Preoperative diagnosis: Suspected acute type A aortic dissection, Marfan syndrome.
Postoperative diagnosis: Acute Stanford type A aortic dissection.

Procedure: Emergency ascending aortic replacement with hemiarch reconstruction and aortic valve resuspension. Cardiopulmonary bypass with hypothermic circulatory arrest.

Intraoperative TEE: intimal flap in the ascending aorta, dilated root, aortic regurgitation.

Findings and course: Median sternotomy. Dissected ascending aorta confirmed. The ascending aorta and proximal arch were replaced with a tube graft (hemiarch). The commissures were resuspended. Post-bypass TEE showed a competent repair with preserved ventricular function. Separated from bypass without difficulty. Chest closed in standard fashion.

Estimated blood loss as recorded by anesthesia. Specimens: ascending aortic wall to pathology. Condition: to cardiac surgical ICU intubated, stable.

Allergies: penicillin, contrast dye.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 11/09/2024   Discharged: 11/19/2024
Service: Cardiac Surgery

Admitting diagnosis: Acute type A aortic dissection.
Discharge diagnoses: Acute type A aortic dissection, status post emergency repair. Aortic regurgitation. Postoperative pericardial effusion, s/p pericardial window. Marfan syndrome. Hypertension.

Procedures:
- 11/09: Emergency ascending aortic replacement with hemiarch and aortic valve resuspension.
- 11/13: Emergency left anterior thoracotomy with pericardial window.

Hospital course: Presented with tearing chest and back pain; diagnosis confirmed by intraoperative TEE and repaired the same day (contrast allergy, no CT). Extubated POD 1. On POD 4 he became hypotensive and tachycardic with a new pericardial effusion and hemodynamic compromise on echo; taken emergently for left anterior thoracotomy and pericardial window with prompt recovery. Drains removed, ambulating independently, tolerating diet. Pain well controlled at discharge.

Discharge medications:
- Metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily (continued)
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily (continued)
- Aspirin 81 mg daily (NEW)

Allergies: Penicillin (rash). Iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Instructions: Sternal precautions, no lifting over 10 lb for 6 weeks, no driving for 4 weeks. Cardiac surgery clinic in about 4 weeks. Follow up with PCP within 1 week. Cardiology aortic clinic for surveillance.

documents.title: Phone Call - Mother
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt's mother called to let us know what happened. Reports Declan was taken to emergency surgery Saturday for a torn aorta at the regional hospital, now in the cardiac ICU, off the breathing tube. Wanted us to know and to cancel anything scheduled. No appts here to cancel; cardiology referral still pending for December. Routed to PCP.

documents.title: PCP Note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Noted. Will request records and see him within a week of discharge. Asked front desk to watch for the discharge summary.

documents.title: Transitional Care Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Post-discharge call, reached pt. Home since yesterday, mother staying with him for a couple weeks. Pain manageable. Incisions dry. No fever, no shortness of breath. Has all three meds including the new aspirin 81, filled at his pharmacy last night. Reviewed when to call 911. Visit booked 11/22 with PCP.

events.reason: Hospital follow-up after aortic dissection repair

documents.title: Post-Hospital Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
POST-DISCHARGE VISIT

Discharge summary and op report reviewed.

S: 3 days home after 10-day stay for acute type A dissection 11/9. Emergency ascending + hemiarch replacement with valve resuspension the same day; on POD 4 needed an emergency L anterior thoracotomy and pericardial window for an effusion. Mother driving him. Sore at both incisions, manageable. Sleeping in a recliner. Walking around the apartment and to the mailbox. No fever, no SOB at rest, no palpitations. Taking metoprolol, lisinopril and the new aspirin.

Meds: metoprolol succinate 50 daily, lisinopril 10 daily, aspirin 81 daily (new).
Allergies: PCN (rash), contrast (hives).

O: Vitals as charted, weight down about 3 kg. Thin, comfortable. Sternotomy well approximated, no drainage, sternum stable. L anterior thoracotomy incision clean and dry. Heart regular. Lungs clear, decreased a bit at the L base. No edema.

A/P:
1. S/p type A dissection repair. Recovering as expected. Sternal precautions and no driving per surgery. Surgery clinic visit next month. Cardiology at the hospital's aortic program will follow him from here, so I'm cancelling the outside cardiology referral we placed in August.
2. HTN. BP nicely controlled. Continue metoprolol and lisinopril.
3. Aspirin 81 started by surgery, continue.
4. CBC/BMP today post-op.

We talked about his dad. He's understandably shaken. Offered to talk more any time.

RTC 2-3 months, sooner prn.

documents.title: Cardiac Surgery Clinic Letter
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — CARDIAC SURGERY CLINIC
Date of visit: 12/19/2024

Dear Doctor,

I saw Mr. Fischer about six weeks after emergency ascending aortic and hemiarch replacement with aortic valve resuspension on 11/09, complicated on 11/13 by a pericardial effusion managed with a left anterior thoracotomy and pericardial window.

He is doing well. Walking daily, pain minimal, back to part-time computer work from home. Both incisions are healed and the sternum is stable. Heart sounds regular. Lungs clear. No edema.

Medications: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily. Allergies: penicillin, iodinated contrast.

Plan: Continue all three medications. He may advance activity and lift gradually over the next several weeks; no heavy straining or competitive sport. Long-term aortic surveillance will be through the cardiology aortic clinic, which he will see in the spring. Return to us as needed.

Thank you for allowing us to participate in his care.

Cardiac Surgery

reports.text: Complete study. Left ventricle normal in size with normal systolic function. Normal wall motion. The ascending aortic graft appears intact. The native aortic root is dilated. Aortic regurgitation is present. Mitral valve unremarkable. Normal right ventricular size and function. No pericardial effusion.
reports.conclusion: Intact ascending aortic graft. Dilated native aortic root. Aortic regurgitation.

documents.title: Cardiology Aortic Clinic Letter
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — CARDIOLOGY, AORTIC CLINIC
Date of visit: 03/06/2025

Dear Colleague,

Mr. Fischer is a 28-year-old with Marfan syndrome, now four months out from emergency ascending aortic and hemiarch replacement with valve resuspension for acute type A dissection (11/2024), course complicated by a pericardial effusion requiring a window. Strong family history: father died of dissection at 42, paternal aunt with prophylactic root replacement.

He feels well and is fully active at a desk job. No chest pain, dyspnea or syncope.

Medications: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: penicillin (rash); iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Exam: Tall, thin. Healed sternotomy. Regular rhythm, soft diastolic murmur at the right upper sternal border. Lungs clear. Radial pulses equal. No edema.

Echo today: ascending graft intact; native aortic root dilated; aortic regurgitation present; normal LV function.

Impression/plan:
1. Marfan syndrome s/p type A dissection repair with residual dilated native root. Continue beta-blocker and ACE inhibitor at current doses; BP goal is being met. Repeat aortic imaging in about a year. Given his contrast allergy, noncontrast imaging will be favored.
2. Aortic regurgitation, followed by echo.
3. Avoid heavy isometric lifting and contact sports; stimulants and decongestants should be avoided.

Thank you for allowing us to share in his care.

Cardiology

events.reason: Dyspnea and hemoptysis after cocaine inhalation

reports.text: Portable AP chest. Diffuse bilateral alveolar opacities. Postoperative sternotomy wires and mediastinal surgical changes. No pneumothorax. No large pleural effusion. Heart size within normal limits.

Flexible bronchoscopy under moderate sedation on high-flow oxygen. Airways inspected to the subsegmental level bilaterally; no endobronchial lesion and no focal bleeding source. Sequential lavage of the right middle lobe: each successive aliquot returned more hemorrhagic than the last.
reports.conclusion: Progressively hemorrhagic sequential lavage consistent with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage. No endobronchial lesion.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL — EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 07/10/2025

CC: trouble breathing, coughing blood

HPI: 29M with Marfan syndrome, s/p emergency type A dissection repair 11/2024, HTN. Friends brought him in from a party tonight; they say he inhaled something they took to be cocaine, and shortly afterward he got acutely short of breath and started bringing up blood. Arrives anxious and sweaty.

Meds: metoprolol succinate 50 daily, lisinopril 10 daily, aspirin 81 daily.
Allergies: penicillin (rash), iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Exam: BP 150/95, HR 110, RR 28, SpO2 88% on room air. Anxious, diaphoretic. Crackles in both lung fields. Healed sternotomy. Otherwise unremarkable.

Data: Hgb 13.2, WBC 12,000, plt 250,000. PT 12 sec (ref 11-13.5), PTT 30 sec (ref 25-35). D-dimer 500 ng/mL (ref <500). Urine tox positive for cocaine metabolites. Portable CXR: diffuse bilateral alveolar infiltrates.

MDM: Hypoxemic respiratory failure with hemoptysis and diffuse alveolar filling after inhaled cocaine; leading concern is cocaine-associated alveolar hemorrhage. Placed on high-flow nasal cannula with improvement in saturation. Aspirin held. ICU consulted.

Disposition: MICU.

documents.title: Addiction Medicine Consult
documents.author: addiction medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — ADDICTION MEDICINE CONSULT
Date: 07/12/2025

Reason: cocaine use with life-threatening complication.

29-year-old man admitted to the ICU with alveolar hemorrhage after inhaling cocaine, on a background of Marfan syndrome and a repaired aortic dissection. Urine toxicology positive for cocaine metabolites. Interviewed at length about his cocaine use; the history meets DSM-5 criteria for stimulant use disorder, cocaine type, severe. Never smoker, drinks rarely.

Assessment: Stimulant use disorder, severe, cocaine.

Recommendations: Motivational interviewing done at bedside; he is ambivalent but engaged. No FDA-approved medication for cocaine use disorder. Recommend outpatient addiction medicine/behavioral treatment; information given. PCP to reinforce.

documents.title: ICU Discharge Summary
documents.author: critical care
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 07/10/2025   Discharged: 07/14/2025
Service: Medical Intensive Care

Diagnoses: Diffuse alveolar hemorrhage, cocaine-associated. Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure, resolved. Stimulant use disorder, severe, cocaine. Marfan syndrome s/p type A dissection repair. Hypertension.

Course: Presented after inhaling cocaine with hemoptysis, hypoxemia (88% RA) and diffuse bilateral alveolar infiltrates. Managed on high-flow nasal cannula in the MICU; never required intubation. Bronchoscopy 7/11: no endobronchial lesion, sequential lavage progressively more hemorrhagic, confirming alveolar hemorrhage. ANCA and anti-GBM antibody negative. Coagulation studies normal. Hemoptysis stopped by day 2, weaned to room air on day 3. Aspirin held during the stay and resumed at discharge. Addiction medicine saw him on 7/12.

Discharge medications (unchanged from admission):
- Metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily
- Aspirin 81 mg daily (resume)

Allergies: Penicillin (rash). Iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Follow-up: PCP within 1 week; repeat chest X-ray in 4-6 weeks; outpatient addiction treatment.

reports.conclusion: Widened mediastinum with prominent aortic knob.

reports.text: Pre-repair: mobile intimal flap in the native aortic root below the prior ascending graft, consistent with Stanford type A dissection. Moderate aortic regurgitation. REGIONAL HOSPITAL — EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT
Date of service: 07/16/2026

CC: chest pain, short of breath

HPI: 30M, Marfan syndrome, emergency ascending/hemiarch repair for type A dissection 11/2024, cocaine-associated alveolar hemorrhage 7/2025, HTN. Sudden severe chest discomfort and difficulty breathing that started about 40 minutes before he arrived. Acknowledges ongoing cocaine use, both injected and snorted.

Meds: metoprolol succinate 50 daily, lisinopril 10 daily, aspirin 81 daily.
Allergies: penicillin (rash), iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Exam: T 37.9 C (100.2 F), HR 112, BP 160/55. Distressed. Left radial pulse markedly weaker than the right and the left arm is cool. Inspiratory crackles throughout both lungs. High-pitched decrescendo diastolic murmur, loudest at the left 3rd intercostal space. No chest wall trauma or wounds.

Data: Portable CXR - widened mediastinum, prominent aortic knob. Bedside echo - moderate AR and a mobile intimal flap in the aorta.

MDM: Recurrent aortic dissection in a patient with Marfan syndrome and prior proximal repair. CT angiography not pursued given contrast allergy and findings already sufficient for surgery; cardiac surgery at bedside, to OR for TEE and repair. Febrile with injection use and a regurgitant murmur: two sets of blood cultures drawn before the OR.

Disposition: OR.

documents.title: Operative Report
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — CARDIAC SURGERY
OPERATIVE REPORT
Date of surgery: 07/16/2026

Preoperative diagnosis: Recurrent acute aortic dissection; Marfan syndrome; status post ascending and hemiarch replacement with valve resuspension (11/2024).
Postoperative diagnosis: Recurrent acute Stanford type A dissection of the native aortic root; moderate aortic regurgitation.

Procedure: Emergency redo median sternotomy. Valve-sparing aortic root replacement (reimplantation technique) with reimplantation of the coronary ostia and anastomosis to the existing ascending graft. Cardiopulmonary bypass.

Intraoperative TEE: pre-repair mobile intimal flap in the native root below the prior graft, moderate AR; post-repair no significant residual AR, normal LV function.

Findings and course: Careful redo sternal entry. Dense adhesions taken down. The native root was dissected below the previous graft. Root excised with the valve preserved, coronary buttons mobilized, and a root graft sewn in with the valve reimplanted inside it. Coronary buttons reimplanted. Distal anastomosis to the existing ascending graft. Weaned from bypass without difficulty. Hemostasis obtained, chest closed.

Condition: to cardiac surgical ICU, intubated, stable.
Allergies: penicillin, iodinated contrast.

documents.title: Discharge Summary
documents.author: cardiac surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL — DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admitted: 07/16/2026   Discharged: 07/25/2026
Service: Cardiac Surgery

Diagnoses: Recurrent acute type A aortic dissection of the native aortic root, status post emergency repair. Aortic regurgitation, corrected. Marfan syndrome. Hypertension. Stimulant use disorder, severe, cocaine.

Procedure: 07/16 emergency redo sternotomy with valve-sparing aortic root replacement (reimplantation).

Course: Presented with acute chest pain and dyspnea; bedside echo showed an intimal flap and moderate AR. Taken directly to the OR; TEE confirmed a type A dissection of the native root below the 2024 graft. Repair as above, post-repair TEE with no significant residual regurgitation. Extubated on POD 1. Blood cultures x2 drawn on arrival: no growth at 5 days. Progressive ambulation, chest tubes out, tolerating diet.

Discharge medications (unchanged):
- Metoprolol succinate ER 50 mg daily
- Lisinopril 10 mg daily
- Aspirin 81 mg daily

Allergies: Penicillin (rash). Iodinated contrast (urticaria).

Instructions: Sternal precautions, no lifting over 10 lb, no driving until cleared. Cardiac surgery clinic in 2-3 weeks. PCP within 1 week. Cardiology aortic clinic after surgical clearance. Cocaine cessation strongly advised.

REGIONAL HOSPITAL — CARDIAC SURGERY CLINIC
Date of visit: 08/13/2026

Dear Doctor,

Mr. Fischer returned four weeks after emergency redo sternotomy with valve-sparing aortic root replacement on 07/16 for a recurrent type A dissection of the native root.

He is recovering well. Sternotomy healing, sternum stable. Heart sounds regular. Lungs clear. No edema.

Medications: metoprolol succinate 50 mg daily, lisinopril 10 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily. Allergies: penicillin, iodinated contrast.

Plan: Continue all three medications. No lifting over 10 lb until we clear him at the next check. Desk work from home is fine. He will be seen in the cardiology aortic clinic for long-term follow-up. We reinforced that cocaine is a direct threat to his aorta.
